title: Bayesian Networks for the Early Warning of Student Dropout in Higher Education
content: The early identification of students at risk of dropping out is central to university tutoring, yet many predictive models are hard for instructors to interpret. This article builds and evaluates a Bayesian network that predicts academic risk in higher education from enrolment information, prioritizing transparency. A quantitative, non-experimental and predictive design was adopted within the field of learning analytics. An open higher-education dataset of 3630 students was used, with eight demographic, socioeconomic and enrolment variables and a binary target distinguishing at-risk students from those who pass. The graph structure was learned through hill-climbing with the Bayesian information criterion, and the conditional probabilities were estimated with a Bayesian estimator; the model was validated on an independent test partition (30%) and through ten-fold cross-validation. The network reached an accuracy of 0.76 and an area under the curve of 0.83, comparable to benchmark classifiers such as naïve Bayes, the decision tree and logistic regression. Payment status, debtor condition, scholarship, age and gender formed the Markov blanket of risk, with estimated probabilities ranging from 10% to 98% depending on the profile. It is concluded that the network provides an interpretable and actionable early-warning system to target tutoring and financial support, with a reproducible and transferable framework for institutional contexts.
